title: shadow-run-performance-sync-summary-2026-06-02
content:
Attendees: Ethan, Priya, Liam, Marina, Jon

Purpose: capture results and next steps from the 2h shadowed workload run against prod traffic (06-02 morning window). Objective was to reproduce the 99th+ latency regression that customer-facing endpoints saw on 2026-05-28 under mixed short/long sequences, and to validate candidate mitigations (sched-affinity tweak + small batch cap).

Run summary:
- Window: 2026-06-02 09:00-11:00 UTC. Shadowed ~12% of live traffic through the canary proxy; no user-visible shuffle, logs sampled at 1/10k for payload.
- Configs tested: A (baseline prod), B (sched-affinity=cpu-pack tight), C (batch cap=8, disable continuous batching for seq>512), D (B+C). Each config ran for 20m with 5m cooldowns.
- Workload mix: 72% short (<64 tokens), 18% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512). 60% chat-like multi-turn (KV-cache warm), 40% single-turn.

Key observations:
- Baseline (A): reproduced 99th increase (~+45ms) relative to last stable baseline; tail spikes correlated with bursts of interleaved long sequences appearing in same GPU worker.
- B only (sched-affinity): 99th reduced by ~22ms vs A, but throughput dropped 4% and some microburst amplification appeared at the 95-97th during medium-length floods.
- C only (batch cap=8): reduced throughput by 6% but smoothed 95th and 99th for long seqs; short-request p50 unaffected.
- D (B+C): best tail performance (99th ~ -18ms from A), throughput -8% vs A, slightly higher CPU utilization on host.
- KV-cache hit-ratio: unchanged between runs, but cache evictions temporarily rose during medium->long transition windows (possibly due to worker-local cache TTL misalignment).

Trace-level notes:
- Traces where spikes occurred show repeated kernel reorder attempts and CUDA stream stalls lasting ~0.8-1.4ms stacking up across tens of tokens. Span IDs: sample traces attached in linked_artifacts.
- Host-side scheduler logs show worker preemption events (nicely correlated with cloud maintenance pings in two hosts). Need to verify correlation vs. true cause.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) In-process scheduling + mixed sequence length leads to token emission microbursts where kernels queue on the same CUDA stream and stall due to stream contention. Sched-affinity reduces cross-talk but increases fragmentation (lower batching).
2) Worker-local KV-cache TTL not aligned across worker pool; when long sequences transition frequently, cache churn causes transient additional work per request (recompilation-like overhead in edge cases).
3) Rare OS-level preemption events amplified by bursty arrival patterns.

Short-term conclusions:
- Combined mitigation (sched-affinity + batch cap) looks promising for tail latency but costs throughput. Trade-off acceptable for SLOs for now; need to quantify economic impact (tokens/sec vs cost).
- Immediate follow-up: schedule controlled A/B for 48h with traffic shaping to be able to compare service-level metrics rather than short-run snapshots.

Action items:
- (Ethan) Draft A/B run plan and rollback criteria. Due: 2026-06-04. JIRA INF-4321 created.
- (Priya) Wire up higher-fidelity trace sampling for long-seq flows (increase sampling to 1/1k for long sequences) and surface example spans in the perf dashboard. Due: 2026-06-05.
- (Liam) Run targeted microbench: stress single-worker with synthetic interleaved short/long sequence pattern, collect CUDA stream metrics and kernel queue lengths. Due: 2026-06-06.
- (Marina) Cost estimate: quantify throughput drop impact on capacity and monthly run-rate for dedicated pools. Due: 2026-06-08.
- (Jon) Verify KV-cache local TTL config across autoscaled workers; propose short patch if mismatch found. Due: 2026-06-05.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact source of sudden kernel reorder calls: is this runtime adaptive behavior or due to model-specific attention kernel fallback? (Follow-up with runtime-research).
- Are preemption events from cloud infra or our own maintenance hooks? (SRE to correlate).
- Is quantization profile interacting with long-seq kernel selection? Unclear — add to model-onboarding checklist.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider introducing soft isolation for long-running sequences: pin long seqs to a small subset of workers with different batching policy; leave short-heavy nodes optimized for throughput.
- Improve worker startup warmup: prefetch KV-cache for known active sessions where possible to reduce churn.

Attachments and artifacts: links above (Jira, PR, traces, dashboard heatmap).

Next sync: quick 30m check-in on A/B readiness on 2026-06-04 16:00 UTC.

If you have additional trace IDs or a run you want replayed under the microbench harness, drop them in #eng-serving-runtime and tag Ethan.
